idea: Track the amount of the pure substance, not the percent. Amount = concentration × volume. Mixing adds amounts and volumes; adding water adds volume only; evaporation removes water only; draining removes both in proportion.
trap: Averaging two concentrations without weighting by volume.
desmos: After you write “acid before plus acid added equals acid after,” any solver finishes it. Writing that equation is the skill.

items.stem: A chemist mixes 60 liters of a 5% salt solution with 40 liters of a 70% salt solution. What is the concentration of salt in the mixture, as a percent?
items.explain: Salt: 0.05(60)+0.7(40)=31 liters, in 100 liters of mixture. The concentration is 10031​=0.31, or 31%. Simply averaging 5% and 70% ignores the different volumes.

items.stem: How many liters of a 55% acid solution must be added to 30 liters of a 5% acid solution to make a 25% acid solution?
items.explain: Acid before plus acid added equals acid after: 0.05(30)+0.55x=0.25(30+x). Then 0.3x=6, so x=20 liters.

items.stem: A 40-liter salt solution is 35% salt. How many liters of water must evaporate for the solution to become 65% salt?
items.explain: Evaporation removes only water, so the salt stays at 0.35(40)=14 liters. At 65%, the total volume is 0.6514​=13280​ liters, so 40−13280​=13240​ liters evaporate.

items.stem: A tank holds 60 liters of a mixture that is 10% antifreeze. Some of the mixture is drained and replaced with the same amount of pure antifreeze, so the tank again holds 60 liters, now 30% antifreeze. How many liters were drained?
items.explain: Draining x liters removes 0.1x liters of antifreeze; adding pure antifreeze puts back x. So 0.1(60)−0.1x+x=0.3(60), which gives 0.9x=12 and x=340​.
